claims: The Artemis II crew splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego.
The Artemis II crew splashed down on Friday, April 10, 2026.
The splashdown occurred at 8:07 p.m. EDT.
The splashdown occurred at 5:07 p.m. PDT.
The splashdown ended a 10-day mission around the moon.
The Orion capsule carried four astronauts.
The Orion capsule endured high-speed re-entry temperatures of nearly 5,000°F.
Navy divers recovered the Orion capsule.
The U.S. Navy assisted in recovering the capsule and crew.
The Artemis II crew consisted of Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
The Artemis II crew is safe.
The Artemis II mission involved a 694,481-mile journey.
Artemis II was the first crewed mission to travel around the moon in over 50 years.
The Artemis II crew was transported to the USS John P. Murtha for medical evaluations.
